erin (support): Hey team — Acme Search escalated, says rerank endpoint returning weird, negative and non-normalized scores across a batch. Posting their payload and sample response now. 

bob_acme (customer): Hi, yeah — our UI shows results with negative numbers and they don't sum or fall in [0,1]. This broke our confidence bar. Example request: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-client-xxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"query":"best espresso machine","candidates":["Breville Barista Express","Ninja Espresso","Cheap $30 pump"]}'
```
And sample response (truncated): 
```json
{"candidates":[{"text":"Breville Barista Express","score":-1.73},{"text":"Ninja Espresso","score":-0.54},{"text":"Cheap $30 pump","score":-6.11}]}
```
We expected probabilities or at least 0-1 scores.

erin (support): Thanks Bob — reassigning to eng-ml, repro steps below. Also note they passed a simple array, no per-candidate IDs.

sophie (eng-ml): Jumping in. Negative scores are expected if the model returns logits or uncalibrated similarity scores. We intentionally return raw scalar scores so customers can choose normalization. Short answer: sort by score DESC; don't assume [0,1]. 

sophie (eng-ml): To verify: is your client trying to average or sum scores across queries? Softmax should be applied across candidates for a single query if you want a probability distribution. Example (Python): 
```python
import math
scores = [-1.73, -0.54, -6.11]
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
# probs ~ [0.20, 0.79, 0.01]
```

bob_acme (customer): Oh wow — we were normalizing per-document using min/max across the whole session which mixed queries. That would explain weird values. But why negatives? Our product team thought negative = error.

sophie (eng-ml): Negative is fine — they're unbounded logits/similarity scores. If you need a 0-1 confidence per result for display, use softmax per candidate set for that single query (or apply a logistic/sigmoid if comparing to a threshold). Do not mix candidates across multiple unrelated queries for normalization. 

raj (eng-platform): Quick check: did the client hit any limits that could cause truncation/invalid inputs? Our rerank endpoint has a per-request candidate limit of 128 and a payload size limit. Also watch out for newline/encoding issues — trailing nulls can change tokenization which affects scores.

bob_acme (customer): We only sent 5 candidates. No truncation. Our logs show sometimes the query had a trailing space and newline from the UI: e.g., "best espresso machine
". Could that change the scores so drastically?

sophie (eng-ml): Yes — whitespace can change tokenization and model activations. But not likely to flip sign across entire set. More likely your normalization step across sessions caused negatives to look odd. Still worth reproducing with their exact payload including whitespace and headers.

erin (support): Bob posted the exact raw request payload and headers in DM. I repro'd locally using their api key (test mode). I got similar raw scores. I then applied softmax per-query and UI looked fine.

bob_acme (customer): Can you paste the exact curl you used to reproduce? Our frontend dev wants to test quickly.

erin (support): Sure — this is what I ran (scrubbed): 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"query":"best espresso machine
","candidates":["Breville Barista Express","Ninja Espresso","Cheap $30 pump"]}'
```
Response (raw): 
```json
{"candidates":[{"text":"Breville Barista Express","score":-1.75},{"text":"Ninja Espresso","score":-0.49},{"text":"Cheap $30 pump","score":-6.05}]}
```
Applying softmax gave normalized probabilities and fixed the UI.

sophie (eng-ml): Actionable items: 
- Documentation update: clarify rerank returns uncalibrated scalar scores (logits/similarity). Recommend softmax/sigmoid examples.
- Support snippet: small code examples in python/js for softmax and descending sort.
- Repro note: confirm whether customers expect calibrated probabilities; consider adding an optional `normalize=true` query param if product team agrees.

erin (support): I'll update the KB with the softmax snippet and link to this thread. Bob — does that solve your immediate issue or do you want a platform-side toggle?

bob_acme (customer): Softmax fix is fine for now. Our PM asked us to request an optional normalized flag so non-engineering teams can avoid writing transforms. If you want a feature request, I'll open one via support portal.

erin (support): Please do file the feature request. We'll track it as a product suggestion (tag: rerank-normalize).

raj (eng-platform): One more technical note for the KB: if you apply softmax on large negative logits you can get underflow; use stable-softmax (subtract max before exp). Example: 
```python
mx = max(scores)
exp = [math.exp(s - mx) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
```

sophie (eng-ml): Also call out that if your use-case is pairwise relevance (score is independent per candidate), softmax may be inappropriate — instead use a calibrated model or per-candidate sigmoid and threshold.

erin (support): Closing loop: Bob confirmed softmax applied on frontend fixed the confidence bar. Marking ESC resolved-for-now; will keep feature request open. :white_check_mark:

bob_acme (customer): Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help! :rocket:
